Helium 2%

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
Around 2 billion years ago South Africa was struck by a very large meteor resulting in a huge crater, the Vredefort Dome ..the world’s largest known crater on earth.

Fast forward a billion or so years, an IT man Nick Mitchell and banker Stefani Marani - who know nothing about minerals or gases - buy a piece of land 187 hectares in an area around Welkom, Virginia and Theunissen in the Free State, that has gas exploration rights. They buy it for US$1.00. Backed by investment from friends and family, the pair took the project on with the intention of generating a small amount of power to Sibanye and Harmony with the existing wells. A side line industry.

They discover from a gas sample that contains 2 % Helium. They know nothing about Helium, it’s what you fill party balloons with! But they do some research and discover it’s critical not only in the making of MRI and CATSCAN machines but also for manufacturing other life saving equipment.



Further information:
So they found out who the big manufacturers were and started approaching them - were they interested in buying their helium? General Electric in New York is the first port of call and yes they are interested. When they say they have 2% Helium in their gas suddenly the conversation ends and there’s no interest.

They phone other well-known companies. Conversations go well until they say 2%. Noone’s interested. When they get to Linde Gas Group in Germany their man says “ I would be rich if I had a dollar every time someone says they have 2 % Helium in their gas you at best have a fraction of a percent.”

How they fake the tests, he said, is to flush out the equipment with Helium first and then when you put the gas in to be tested it shows high results. So even if you have been told the tests show 2% Helium it’s a lie. It was at this point they told him that the test was done in one of their own labs based in Joburg.
There was silence on the other end of the phone…he said we’ll get back to you. A few days later a senior executive out of Germany calls Stefano up asking about the 2%, did they think it was real?
“We don’t know” Stefano replied “ you were the ones telling us we had 2% in our gas.” So they asked if they could fly some scientists our from Germany, which they promptly did 2 weeks later.
The results were absolutely correct. They did have 2 % Helium in their gas. What ensued from there was a very quick negotiation with the head of the Helium division in NY.
This is the first agreement for their vital gas, which will put SA in the position from being a 100% importer of this gas to becoming the 8th country in the world to export Helium.
To put this in perspective, there are only 7 (now 8) countries in the world that produce Helium. The varying degrees of Helium in the gas stream range from Qatar with the lowest concentration of 0,0001 % all the way through to the USA with the highest concentration 0.5%. And that’s considered Helium Rock Star territory!!

The pair signed a deal with Linde gas and called their company Renergen.

The Geology behind this discovery

The geology is as unique as the story of how the company came into being. Around 2 billion years ago South Africa was struck by a very large meteor, which was responsible for bringing almost all of earth’s platinum which is why the country is so rich in the metal. The meteor left a large crater which filled with organic matter over time, which bacteria began feeding on. Today, that organic matter is very deep, and the bacteria are still thriving, meaning that the natural gas coming to the surface is part of an ongoing biological process making the gas completely renewable. Furthermore, the meteor left behind a large amount of uranium, which is responsible for the generation of helium and also the reason why this find is the richest helium deposit in the world.

Scientists and geologists from Toronto University, Professor Barbara Sherwood and Edinburgh, Prof Gilfillan and in South Africa, Prof Terence McCarthy are very interested in this unique phenomenon unique because the gas wells themselves regenerate. A gas well will usually only last 15 years. Their wells that were drilled in the 50’s and 60’s are producing still. The way they determined they determined the gas containing the helium was regenerative was by looking at carbon isotopes/carbon dating.
The gas is compressed into Liquefied Natural Gas (LGN) and is used as a substitute for diesel, and can significantly reduce the carbon footprint, buy up to 90% of green house gas emissions, relative to diesel.
In 2016, they ran a pilot project with Megabus. Megabus invested R25 million on 10 buses that run exclusively on natural gas from their one well They used these buses to transport mine workers and school children in the area. The project was highly successful as a proof of concept, showing significant cost reductions to the bus operator, as well as reducing carbon emissions by more than 2.6 million kilograms.

Then in December 2019 hitting a fissure by mistake they discovered gas which has 12 % Helium concentrate making it without doubt the richest source of Helium in the world and amazing economic story for South Africa.

Why is Helium so important? It’s not only used in manufacturing life-saving equipment and cat scans but a world without helium would mean a world without TV, cell phones , computers, micro chips , high end electronics , fibre optic cables, we couldn’t launch rockets or satellites, no nuclear energy…

About one third of the world helium was supplied annually by a strategic storage facility in the United States built after World War I. In 2018 the facility declared the helium had been used up which has led to critical supply shortages, with many hospitals globally running out and not being able to conduct MRIs. That same year President Trump signed a declaratory order deeming helium as critical to US National Security, following which a US agency, the Overseas Private Investment Corporation or OPIC, then invested R600m into Renergen in order to ensure this project would come online and begin delivering this critical commodity.

Press Release:


The Magic of Helium
Ask any ordinary person what the purpose of helium is and they will probably say it’s to fill party balloons. It is however one of the world's most critical gases, an essential component in life-saving technologies like MRIs and CAT scans. But global supplies have been dwindling, until the recent discovery of astonishingly rich helium wells in the Free State. Meet the two investors who now sit on one of the richest helium concentrations recorded globally.
Producer: Diana Lucas | Presenter: Claire Mawisa


Script:


V/O
Around 2 billion years ago, planet earth was struck by an asteroid …. Resulting in the Vredefort Dome, the world’s largest known crater.

Link: Fast forward a billion or so years, an IT man and a banker buy a piece of land, around Virginia in the Free State that has gas exploration rights and some wells on it. They are looking at starting a small side line business to supply natural gas as a substitute to diesel to mines in the area.

Nick: We saw this rusted pipe sticking out the ground, there was something blowing from within, we were told this was methane and we said this was a great idea.

V/O
Nick Mitchell and Stef Marani bought the land in 2013. With the gas exploration rights from neighbouring farms the area measures 187 thousand hectares.

Stefano The idea was quiet simple, it was rent a few gas power generators put then on top of the well heads, feed power back into the one of goldmines nearby. It was literally going to be a tiny little project,

V/O
In the course of doing the deal, a gas sample of was required……

Nick: So in a panic we drove down and collected samples drove back immediately to the labs and we had them analysed.

V/O
The lab results showed a concentration of 2 % Helium in their methane gas.

Link: All Stef and Nick knew about Helium is that it’s a gas used in balloons to make them float.so they started researching and discovered how vital Helium is in our modern world.

Stef: I am looking at this piece of paper and it says 2% helium, I ask Nick what do you know about Helium and he says balloons and we ask Dr Google.

Nick What we discovered first was MRI’s, an MRI cat scan can’t operate without Helium.

V/O
So they researched who the manufacturers of the MRI’s are so they could sell their Helium to them.

Stef : We eventually cold call someone in New York. and they ask how much Helium and we say 2% and the conversation ends….. so we then phone another gas company we get to the 2% mark and the conversation ends.

Nick: But I suppose we are quiet persistent our last call was to LInde the industrial gas supplies company and we spoke to one of the engineers in Germany and he said you know if I had a $ every time someone said they had these results he’d be rich

Stef : .You don’t have Helium in your gas its too rare.

Nick: So we said that’s quiet interesting, it was your lab that ran these samples.

V/O ( Renergen has a soft g )
Linde HQ sent out some of their scientists to re run the tests…. It was confirmed Renergen, Stef and Nick’s company had 2 % Helium……..

Nick: Stef and I looked across at each other, we didn’t say anything we were too cool and calm for that, but we knew we’ve got something quiet special on our hands here,

V/O
Helium is not only critical in the manufacture of life-saving equipment, but a world without helium would mean a world without TV, cell phones, computers, micro chips. We couldn’t launch rockets or satellites.

Stef: It’s pretty fundamental to every aspect,so the consequences of not having Helium are pretty far reaching.

V/O
To put this in perspective, there are only 7 countries, now 8 including South Africa, that produce Helium.

Stef: The lowest concentration is Qatar, they are extracting it at around 0.01%, the United States is around is around 0.35%, they are the Helium rock stars. Now all of a sudden you have a field where the worst well is 2%.

V/O
The reason for the high concentration of Helium goes back to around 2 billion years to the asteroid strike.

Prof. Emeritus Terence McCarthy
Wits: School of Geosciences

Prof : There was a humungous explosion it was so intense the rocks were forced down initially and then they squirted back up because of the intensity of the explosion the rocks behave like water they solidify quiet quickly so they trapped the shape.

V/O
Leading expert on the geology of South Africa, Prof Terence McCarthy finds this Vredefort area a treasure trove.

Prof Terence McCarthy: These rocks that lie under the Vredefort Structure that folded down and preserved contained a lot of gold and a lot of uranium. This massive meteorite impact that sucked these rocks down under into this hollow and protected them from later erosion… and kept them secure. It’s Just one of these miracles and that’s why this deposit has produced 40 % of all the gold ever mined in history.

V/O
Bacteria, incorporated into the rock, survived, producing methane gas, and the uranium which is decaying into lead is producing Helium.

Prof Terence McCarthy: Along the way the way they give off bullets of Helium … and because of the structure that Vredefort crated that deep enfolding can’t escape, the Helium slowly migrates into little cracks fissures

V/O
And together with the Methane, the Helium travelling through the cracks reaches the surface.

Link: In the world of geology this is a unique phenomenon. Usually a gas well will last 15 years but here wells that were drilled in the 50’s and 60’s are still producing helium bearing gas.

Stef : This well is an average producer for us and it blowing at the same rate since 1972. This has produced over 200 000 kg’s Helium and there has not been a decline in the concentration of this Helium.

V/O
What makes this discovery miraculous, is the fact that the Helium is part of an ongoing biological process… making the gas completely renewable.

Claire: Will the Helium continue to be produced?
Prof: It will regenerate but we can’t say if it will happen at the same rate that we continue to extract…in the meantime resources are huge we’ve only just started.

V/O
This comes at a time when there is a worldwide Helium crisis. The United States government’s strategic reserve, the Bureau of Land Management, has virtually run dry of their stockpiled Helium.

Stef: The BLM is now empty, that was 30% of the worlds helium supply in any given year.…..shortly after that we got funding from the US government they gave us a loan of 40 million US $ to to test the feasibility of extracting Helium from SA.

NicK: Helium is a super critical element any source known to the world and the market has got attention on it. Ours happens to be a source with the worlds highest concentrations recorded.

Claire: We are all considered about harming the environment is extracting the helium doing any damage to surrounding areas??
Prof: No, No It’s a win win thing you simply drill a hole and let it flow out on its own the trick is to drill a hole in the right place, and that is a challenge. The gas its so light it escapes through the atmosphere.

V/O
In December last year, Renergen made another off the chart discovery.

Nick……by fate and chance we intersected a fault, as we started to pull equipment out so we could go in a more lateral position, the sensors went off the charts.

Sf: And we hit by accident a fault we didn’t know existed… where you have Helium coming in at 12 %. If you are mining for gold and you are used to mining for gold at 5 grams per ton it would be like finding gold at 1 000g per ton.

V/O
Two businessmen, who seven years ago knew so little about Helium, now have the richest commercial recoverable source of this precious commodity …

Stef: I think sometimes it’s the lack of knowledge of what you’re getting into that helps with the discovery in the first place.

V/O
And South Africa becomes a major supplier of this critical gas.

Stef: We become an exporter of Helium instead of an ….that means we ae now receiving cash as opposed to paying cash out. From a scientific perspective it’s important because we are now a Helium producer in a very exclusive club, We were at a Conference 2018 in Houston you had 98 % of entire worlds suppliers 95 consumers and all equipment manufactures 300 people exclusive little now SA joined.

Nick : Its evolved slowly, definitely bigger then the first day we saw this rusted pipe. Do we think its reached its pinnacle absolutely not, we are just taking one day at a time.






Nick : Its evolved slowly, definitely bigger then the first day we saw this rusted pipe. Do we think its reached its pinnacle

Prof Terence McCarthy: Along the way the way they give off bullets of Helium … and because of the structure that Vredefort crated that deep enfolding can’t escape, the Helium slowly migrates into little cracks fissures V/O And together with the Methane, the Helium travelling through the cracks reaches the surface. Link: In the world of geology this is a unique phenomenon. Usually a gas well will last 15 years but here wells that were drilled in the 50’s and 60’s are still producing helium bearing gas. Stef : This well is an average producer for us and it blowing at the same rate since 1972. This has produced over 200 000 kg’s Helium and there has not been a decline in the concentration of this Helium. V/O What makes this discovery miraculous, is the fact that the Helium is part of an ongoing biological process… making the gas completely renewable. Claire: Will the Helium continue to be produced? Prof: It will regenerate but we can’t say if it will happen at the same rate that we continue to extract…in the meantime resources are huge we’ve only just started. V/O This comes at a time when there is a worldwide Helium crisis. The United States government’s strategic reserve, the Bureau of Land Management, has virtually run dry of their stockpiled Helium. Stef: The BLM is now empty, that was 30% of the worlds helium supply in any given year.…..shortly after that we got funding from the US government they gave us a loan of 40 million US $ to to test the feasibility of extracting Helium from SA. NicK: Helium is a super critical element any source known to the world and the market has got attention on it. Ours happens to be a source with the worlds highest concentrations recorded. Claire: We are all considered about harming the environment is extracting the helium doing any damage to surrounding areas?? Prof: No, No It’s a win win thing you simply drill a hole and let it flow out on its own the trick is to drill a hole in the right place, and that is a challenge. The gas its so light it escapes through the atmosphere. V/O In December last year, Renergen made another off the chart discovery. Nick……by fate and chance we intersected a fault, as we started to pull equipment out so we could go in a more lateral position, the sensors went off the charts. Sf: And we hit by accident a fault we didn’t know existed… where you have Helium coming in at 12 %. If you are mining for gold and you are used to mining for gold at 5 grams per ton it would be like finding gold at 1 000g per ton. V/O Two businessmen, who seven years ago knew so little about Helium, now have the richest commercial recoverable source of this precious commodity … Stef: I think sometimes it’s the lack of knowledge of what you’re getting into that helps with the discovery in the first place. metadata.Summary: Around 2 billion years ago South Africa was struck by a very large meteor resulting in a huge crater, the Vredefort Dome ..the world’s largest known crater on earth. Fast forward a billion or so years, an IT man Nick Mitchell and banker Stefani Marani - who know nothing about minerals or gases - buy a piece of land 187 hectares in an area around Welkom, Virginia and Theunissen in the Free State, that has gas exploration rights. They buy it for US$1.00. Backed by investment from friends and family, the pair took the project on with the intention of generating a small amount of power to Sibanye and Harmony with the existing wells. A side line industry. They discover from a gas sample that contains 2 % Helium. They know nothing about Helium, it’s what you fill party balloons with! But they do some research and discover it’s critical not only in the making of MRI and CATSCAN machines but also for manufacturing other life saving equipment.
metadata.Further information: So they found out who the big manufacturers were and started approaching them - were they interested in buying their helium? General Electric in New York is the first port of call and yes they are interested. When they say they have 2% Helium in their gas suddenly the conversation ends and there’s no interest. They phone other well-known companies. Conversations go well until they say 2%. Noone’s interested. When they get to Linde Gas Group in Germany their man says “ I would be rich if I had a dollar every time someone says they have 2 % Helium in their gas you at best have a fraction of a percent.” How they fake the tests, he said, is to flush out the equipment with Helium first and then when you put the gas in to be tested it shows high results. So even if you have been told the tests show 2% Helium it’s a lie. It was at this point they told him that the test was done in one of their own labs based in Joburg. There was silence on the other end of the phone…he said we’ll get back to you. A few days later a senior executive out of Germany calls Stefano up asking about the 2%, did they think it was real? “We don’t know” Stefano replied “ you were the ones telling us we had 2% in our gas.” So they asked if they could fly some scientists our from Germany, which they promptly did 2 weeks later. The results were absolutely correct. They did have 2 % Helium in their gas. What ensued from there was a very quick negotiation with the head of the Helium division in NY. This is the first agreement for their vital gas, which will put SA in the position from being a 100% importer of this gas to becoming the 8th country in the world to export Helium. To put this in perspective, there are only 7 (now 8) countries in the world that produce Helium. The varying degrees of Helium in the gas stream range from Qatar with the lowest concentration of 0,0001 % all the way through to the USA with the highest concentration 0.5%. And that’s considered Helium Rock Star territory!! The pair signed a deal with Linde gas and called their company Renergen. The Geology behind this discovery The geology is as unique as the story of how the company came into being. Around 2 billion years ago South Africa was struck by a very large meteor, which was responsible for bringing almost all of earth’s platinum which is why the country is so rich in the metal. The meteor left a large crater which filled with organic matter over time, which bacteria began feeding on. Today, that organic matter is very deep, and the bacteria are still thriving, meaning that the natural gas coming to the surface is part of an ongoing biological process making the gas completely renewable. Furthermore, the meteor left behind a large amount of uranium, which is responsible for the generation of helium and also the reason why this find is the richest helium deposit in the world. Scientists and geologists from Toronto University, Professor Barbara Sherwood and Edinburgh, Prof Gilfillan and in South Africa, Prof Terence McCarthy are very interested in this unique phenomenon unique because the gas wells themselves regenerate. A gas well will usually only last 15 years. Their wells that were drilled in the 50’s and 60’s are producing still. The way they determined they determined the gas containing the helium was regenerative was by looking at carbon isotopes/carbon dating. The gas is compressed into Liquefied Natural Gas (LGN) and is used as a substitute for diesel, and can significantly reduce the carbon footprint, buy up to 90% of green house gas emissions, relative to diesel. In 2016, they ran a pilot project with Megabus. Megabus invested R25 million on 10 buses that run exclusively on natural gas from their one well They used these buses to transport mine workers and school children in the area. The project was highly successful as a proof of concept, showing significant cost reductions to the bus operator, as well as reducing carbon emissions by more than 2.6 million kilograms. Then in December 2019 hitting a fissure by mistake they discovered gas which has 12 % Helium concentrate making it without doubt the richest source of Helium in the world and amazing economic story for South Africa. Why is Helium so important? It’s not only used in manufacturing life-saving equipment and cat scans but a world without helium would mean a world without TV, cell phones , computers, micro chips , high end electronics , fibre optic cables, we couldn’t launch rockets or satellites, no nuclear energy… About one third of the world helium was supplied annually by a strategic storage facility in the United States built after World War I. In 2018 the facility declared the helium had been used up which has led to critical supply shortages, with many hospitals globally running out and not being able to conduct MRIs. That same year President Trump signed a declaratory order deeming helium as critical to US National Security, following which a US agency, the Overseas Private Investment Corporation or OPIC, then invested R600m into Renergen in order to ensure this project would come online and begin delivering this critical commodity.
